newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Nov housing completions rose 2.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Nov housing completions rose 2.1 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department report on completions of new privately-owned housing units, seasonally adjusted annual rates, in 1,000s, with percent changes from prior months and year over year.
Housing completions by region, seasonally adj., in 1,000s:
The department said the 2.1 percent increase in November housing completions was the largest since May, when they rose 4.3 percent.

Completions of single-family homes rose 0.4 percent in November after a revised 0.1 percent drop in October and a revised 2.9 percent decrease in September. Previously, the department said single-family completions were unchanged in October and down 3.4 percent in September.

November multi-family unit completions rose 9.8 percent after a revised 5.4 percent drop in October and a revised 11.9 percent decrease in September. Previously, the department said October multi-family unit completions fell 3.5 percent and that September multi-family unit completions were off 12.6 percent.

The department said actual completions on an unadjusted basis fell in November to 119,600 units from 129,700 units in October and 122,100 units in September. In November 1995, actual completions were reported at 116,000.

Privately-owned housing units under construction rose to a seasonally adjusted 837,000 in November from 827,000 in October and 826,000 in September. They compare with 790,000 units under construction in November 1995.
